angle: Movement translation, DL (clearest of five groups screened): each rusher's tracked Combine 40 start (speed every 0.1 s from first movement, 0-1.5 s) laid over his own random NFL pass-rush starts from game_frames_sample on one clock; per-player Carry-over tested against pressure rate beyond draft pick, weight and role, in sample, out of class and as calibration against the no-tracking forecast.
metric_name: Carry-over: NFL first step (mean speed 0.3-0.5 s after first movement on random NFL pass-rush starts, alignment-adjusted) minus Combine 40 first step, each in sd after weight and EDGE share
headline_number: After weight and role the 40 start previews the NFL first step at rho 0.07 [90%: -0.14, 0.28], permutation p 0.59 (n = 67); carry-over vs pressure beyond pick 0.18 [-0.10, 0.43], p 0.25 (n = 52), held-out R2 change -0.114. The NFL first step itself sorts direction: top vs bottom third beat the out-of-class forecast 61% vs 13% (Fisher p 0.002), 65% vs 14% with the window chosen leave-one-class-out, but the clean 2025 top third went 2 of 7 (posterior predictive p 0.04 under the 2023-24 rate).
what_changed_from_previous: Revision of round-8 cand_3 (same angle), fixing its two fatal flaws: all four figures are produced by analysis.py and present, and the piece is 1,911 words by wc (1,675 by check.py). Applied the round-8 judges' top_changes: actions and Combine-protocol ask up top; motivation section; lede softened to 'a lead worth a film check, not a rule'; one ledger table of every estimate, interval, n, the null it tests and its p (within-class permutation, max-over-windows, Fisher), replacing scattered p-values; base rate shown as 24 of 69; leave-one-class-out choice of the first-step window; 2025 clean test as a posterior predictive probability; plus-call vs no-call raw pressure table split by EDGE and interior with n; decision card with plus, minus-flag and film-first calls and a same-slot swap (Gillotte vs Umanmielen, picks 66 and 77) plus a pre-registered 2026 rule; official 40 time vs tracked start contrast. Figures: three-row hero with 14-17 pt text and real rush counts; single-message out-of-class panel with off-axis arrows and per-class hollow markers; carry-over map with fixed colorbar and label collisions; group table cut to one sentence.
open_risks: The headline is a null for the angle's question (translation adds nothing beyond pick); judges may read it as another 'tracking adds ~0' audit

The only positive signal (NFL first step sorting who beats the forecast) is driven by 2023-24; the clean 2025 class went 2 of 7, and as a linear term the NFL first step lowers held-out R2 (2024 dominated by Maason Smith)
Season NGS get-off already captures most of the NFL first step (0.40 vs 0.12 beyond it), so the pro-personnel use is a tie-break at most
The first-step window was read off the payoff curve (best-of-13 p 0.13) and the leave-one-class-out window moves between folds (0.3, 0.5, 1.3 s)
Game sample has no blockers, ball or scheme; about 20 random starts per rusher; DL chosen after seeing five groups
